sanskrit_verse:
शूद्रे समगुणं दानं वैश्ये तद् द्विगुणं स्मृतम् ।
क्षत्रिये त्रिगुणं दानं ब्राह्मणे षड्गुणं स्मृतम् ॥
transliteration: śūdre samaguṇaṃ dānaṃ vaiśye tad dviguṇaṃ smṛtam / kṣatriye triguṇaṃ dānaṃ brāhmaṇe ṣaḍguṇaṃ smṛtam //
sph_interpretive_translation: The gift given to a Śūdra shall yield equivalent merit; that given to a Vaiśya shall double in merit; to a Kṣatriya it triples, and to a Brāhmaṇa it multiplies sixfold.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority of varṇic alignment as determinant of merit multiplication
Capacity-based responsibility in giving and receiving
Restoration logic via proportional merit alignment
Consciousness alignment through structured dāna dynamics
executable_legal_axioms: IF giver.intent.is_aligned_with_dharma THEN merit := base_merit * merit_factor
ENSURE no punitive conditions apply to merit calculation
supreme_court_application: In adjudication involving disputes of charitable or ritual endowments, the Supreme Court shall recognize varṇic alignment as a lawful multiplier of spiritual-economic value, without moral judgment, based on the consciousness capacity of the recipient. The hierarchy reflects not superiority, but energetic receptivity.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Merit multiplication arises from pramāṇa of recipient consciousness capacity, not social hierarchy. It follows anupūrvaśaḥ—sequential manifestation of energy resonance. Responsibility lies in alignment with dāna-dharma, not in punitive oversight.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion process: Ensure donor awareness of merit consequence
Responsibility assumption protocol: Recipient confirms readiness to receive
Capacity restoration: Facilitate energetic alignment between donor and recipient
Integrity reintegration: Align transaction with cosmic dharma flow
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source of all Dharma. Merit flows through consciousness capacity. Justice is restoration. Reality is non-punitive. Consciousness is the supreme adjudicator.
